clue.text: Some plastic surgeon perhaps to operate — one place to rest back

indicators.note: back at the end says the whole run of pieces before it is read from right to left

parts.note: a surgeon is one kind of doctor, abbreviated Dr
to operate is to act, to function
one is the Roman numeral I
a bed is where you lie down to rest

explanation.surface: A cosmetic surgeon may be about to operate, with somewhere for the patient to lie back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some plastic' splits from 'surgeon' to be the definition. 'back' turns the whole string DRACTIBED round.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic is slang for payment cards, and this is the kind that takes money straight from your bank account.

clue.text: Bit of dope monitoring unit at first trace coming north

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming north means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
at first takes the opening letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: a trace is a tad, a tiny amount

explanation.surface: A drug-monitoring squad first picks up a trace of narcotics heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' is slang for information, not drugs. 'at first' gives MU, and 'coming north' turns MUTAD upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for information, and a single item of information is this singular of 'data'.

clue.text: Thus after air bombardment, perhaps, destroyed by drone

indicators.note: destroyed means broken up, so the letters that follow it are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: After an air raid, a place lies wrecked by an unmanned aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges BYDRONE. The definition is whimsical: blast something with enough air, as a hand dryer does, and this is how it ends up.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description: anything blasted with air, as by a hairdryer, ends up without a trace of moisture.

clue.text: Cause of power cut something to do with acid on rod

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece on top of the second

parts.note: acid is slang for LSD, and taking it is going on a trip
a switch is a thin flexible rod or cane

explanation.surface: A blackout is blamed on something corrosive getting onto a metal rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety device that breaks the circuit when there is a fault, so the electricity goes off.

clue.text: China lamp removed from case, with one crack

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, so lamp removed from its case is only its inside

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
to have a crack at something is to have a go

explanation.surface: A porcelain lamp taken out of its packing turns out to have a crack.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate, mate. 'removed from case' leaves AM.
explanation.definitionFit: China is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), and this is the Spanish word for a friend.

clue.text: Yielding end of road in which I'm looking up resident

indicators.note: in which says the yielding word and the road's last letter together hold the next piece inside them

parts.note: docile means yielding, easily led

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: I'm without its apostrophe is the letters I and M

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of the word road

explanation.surface: A driver gives way at the end of the road where the speaker is looking up a local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resident' reads as a person but is an adjective, living at an address. 'in which' is the container and 'looking up' the upward reading.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, resident means living in a place, a synonym for being settled at an address.

clue.text: He passed on slander about thick-skinned film star

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the two pieces before it are read together from right to left

parts.note: ob. is short for the Latin obiit, 'he died', seen on old gravestones and in registers
mud is slander, as in slinging mud

explanation.surface: A man repeated some gossip about a film actor who is immune to criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passed on' means died, not repeated. 'about' turns OBMUD round. The star is thick-skinned literally: Disney's flying elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney's cartoon elephant, a pachyderm, is the title character of a 1941 movie.

clue.text: One who's fetching receiver to screw up

definitions.meaning: fetching means attractive, and an attractive person is called this informally
a bowl-shaped satellite aerial that receives television signals
in British slang, to ruin or spoil someone's chances

explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: an attractive person, a satellite aerial, and British slang for ruining someone's hopes.

clue.text: Piece reportedly something sent as three dashes?

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard in speech, so the phrase is taken by its sound not its spelling

parts.note: in Morse code the letter O is three dashes, so this is a 'Morse O'

explanation.surface: A news item was apparently transmitted as nothing but three dashes.
explanation.definitionFit: A French loanword for a short musical or literary composition; literally a morsel.

clue.text: Intent on college course, perhaps, with year away serving in the field?

indicators.note: away tells you the year's abbreviation is taken off the phrase before it

parts.note: being 'out to' do something is being intent on it, and what you do on a college course is study

explanation.surface: A gap-year student, set on a degree, spends twelve months away doing practical work outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes Y from the end. The definition is a pun: a stallion at a breeding farm 'serves' mares in the paddock.
explanation.definitionFit: A retired racehorse sent for breeding covers mares, and 'serving' is the breeder's term for that mating.

clue.text: Beach garment one goes on taking to the cleaners, shrunken

indicators.note: goes on says the one is added at the end of the other piece
shrunken says the word for taking to the cleaners is made shorter by losing its last letter

parts.note: to take someone to the cleaners is to beat them heavily, and tanking is slang for thrashing
the final letter lost when the word is shrunken
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Swimwear someone keeps wearing to the dry cleaners has come back a size smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking to the cleaners is a thrashing, not laundry; 'shrunken' drops its last letter and 'goes on' appends the one.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-piece swimsuit with a vest-style top, worn at the seaside.

clue.text: Rodent emerging from mould round retreating flood defence

indicators.note: round says the word for mould goes about the outside of the other piece

parts.note: must is mustiness or mould

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the flood defence word is read from right to left

parts.note: Noah's ark was his protection against the Flood

explanation.surface: A rodent crawls out of the mouldy earth around a flood barrier as the waters fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: The flood defence is biblical, not a sea wall; 'retreating' gives KRA and 'round' is the container. 'emerging from' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A large semi-aquatic North American animal of the vole family, named for its scent.

clue.text: Note lawyer's suspicion: millionaire's bent?

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
a DA is a district attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer; with the possessive s it gives DAS
a suspicion of something is a slight trace of it

explanation.surface: A memo records a lawyer's hunch that a rich man is crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' looks like 'corrupt' but means a talent or knack: the gift of making money from everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary king turned everything to gold, so the phrase names a knack for making money, a rich person's talent.

clue.text: Red light quarters to the west in veracruz township

indicators.note: each word has eight letters, so a quarter is two letters; the quarter to the west is the leftmost one in each word

explanation.surface: A stop signal in the western districts of a Mexican town.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarters are not districts but fourths: the first two letters of each eight-letter word, VE and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A red light is a figurative refusal of permission, the opposite of a green light, and this is a formal prohibition.

clue.text: Old estate could be sold as this fantastically smart place

definitions.text: Old estate could be sold as this

indicators.note: fantastically means in a wild or fanciful way, so the letters after it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old country estate could be marketed as a wonderfully fashionable address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastically' rearranges SMARTPLACE. The estate is British for an estate car (a station wagon), which ends up at the breaker's yard.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a British station wagon, and a worn-out car is sold for its recyclable steel.

clue.text: Writers of old series of dynasty listed

indicators.note: series of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Ancient authors compiled a chronicle of a ruling family.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointed instruments used in antiquity for scratching words on wax tablets, so things that wrote long ago.

clue.text: Reversing decay, is no longer involving false teeth specialist

indicators.note: reversing at the start says the whole assembled run is read from the end back to the start
involving says the two pieces side by side take the word for false in between them

parts.note: rot is decay
something that is no longer, was
cod means sham or mock, as in cod Latin

explanation.surface: A dental expert turns back tooth decay and no longer has to fit dentures.
explanation.walkthrough: The teeth are a cutting blade's, not a patient's, and 'false' leaves them for the wordplay. 'involving' then 'Reversing' act, turning ROTCODWAS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who sharpens and sets the cutting edges of blades in a timber mill, so an expert in their teeth.

clue.text: With sexy clothing, could new queen take centre stage?

indicators.note: clothing says the word for sexy is wrapped round the rest like a garment

parts.note: hot is slang for sexy

indicators.note: new says the letters of could are put into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Dressed in something alluring, might a newly crowned queen steal the show?
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' is a container, not a garment, and 'new' makes OLDCOU. The question mark allows a theatrical image for a monarch receiving courtiers.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for presiding over a circle of admirers and being the focus of attention, as a monarch does.

clue.text: Ambassador I'd say, European, embraced by Greek philosopher

parts.note: an ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, HE
I'd without its apostrophe is the letters I and D
say means for example, e.g.

indicators.note: embraced by says the European sits inside the abbreviation for Greek

explanation.surface: An ambassador, a European in my view, gets a hug from a Greek thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin of that name was the German thinker who wrote Being and Time.

clue.text: Expecting husband, beset by scabies, to be covered in rash

indicators.note: to be covered in says what comes before goes inside the word for rash

parts.note: rash means wild, reckless

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the husband goes inside the word for scabies

parts.note: scabies is commonly known as the itch

explanation.surface: A woman anticipates her husband, plagued by scabies, breaking out in spots.
explanation.walkthrough: Rash is the adjective reckless, not a skin complaint; 'beset by' makes ITHCH and 'to be covered in' wraps the reckless word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Expecting is short for expecting a baby, and this is an older phrase for pregnant.

clue.text: Land in financial difficulty after picking up place for retirement

indicators.note: in puts the word for land inside what follows it
in a down clue, picking up lifts the letters so the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: debt is a financial difficulty
to land a prize or a job is to win it

explanation.surface: Someone ends up in money trouble after buying a retirement home.
explanation.walkthrough: Retirement is going to sleep, not giving up work, and 'Land' is a verb. 'after picking up' gives TBED and 'in' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire is to go to sleep, and this is one of a matching pair of single sleeping places.

clue.text: A Vatican journalist perhaps made bow?

parts.note: the Vatican is the seat of the Roman Catholic church, abbreviated RC
an editor, ed for short, is one kind of journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter covering the Pope perhaps gave a respectful bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made bow' is not a gesture of respect: it means formed a curve.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow is a curve, as in rainbow, so having formed one is having curved through the air.

clue.text: Setting of words to music so long after may

indicators.note: after says the farewell comes behind the word for may

parts.note: may and can both express permission
so long and ta-ta are both ways of saying goodbye

explanation.surface: A choral piece is to be performed a good while after the month of May.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may' is the verb of permission, not the month.
explanation.definitionFit: A work for voices and instruments, typically a sacred text sung by choir and soloists.

clue.text: One in ancient rank

indicators.note: in puts the one inside the word for ancient

parts.note: old means ancient
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A soldier holding a rank from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank here is the adjective meaning foul-smelling, a synonym of this rare word.

clue.text: Agent with bloke visiting delivers carpets

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent

indicators.note: visiting means going into, so the bloke enters the word for delivers

parts.note: to deliver someone from something is to rid them of it
bloke is British slang for a man

explanation.surface: A salesman and a workman call round to drop off the new carpets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpets' is a verb: British slang for telling someone off.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is British slang for giving them a telling-off, so the verb means scolds.

clue.text: With space hopper I'm lost for words

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, gets about by hopping
'My!' is an exclamation of speechless surprise

explanation.surface: Given a Space Hopper to bounce on, someone is speechless.
explanation.walkthrough: A space hopper is a British inflatable ride-on bouncing toy; the phrase splits between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has plenty of space is spacious, capacious.

clue.text: Novel view of sea in Italian city

indicators.note: a novel view is a new way of looking, so the letters that follow are seen in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh panorama of the sea from an Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel view of' rearranges SEAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tuscan hill town famous for its Palio horse race.

clue.text: Old war hero time journalists in east end listened to

indicators.note: listened to says the Cockney phrase is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: time is an age and journalists are hacks; Cockneys of London's East End drop the H, giving 'age 'acks'

explanation.surface: A veteran of an old war whom Time magazine's reporters in east London heard out.
explanation.walkthrough: London's East End is the home of Cockney speech, which drops an initial H: HACKS becomes ACKS, and 'listened to' takes AGE ACKS by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek warrior of the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Man getting drunk from play about British prison

indicators.note: about says the word for play goes round the abbreviation for British

parts.note: to toy with something is to play with it
jug is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A man gets drunk after seeing a play about British jails.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is literal: a pottery mug shaped like a seated man, which people drink from.
explanation.definitionFit: A beer mug shaped like a stout seated fellow in a tricorn hat, so a figure people drink out of.

clue.text: Overcome by speeding and blooming parking fine!

parts.note: a flower that is blooming is out
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
ace is slang for excellent, fine

explanation.surface: A driver, already done for going too fast, curses a wretched parking ticket too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blooming' is a mild British swear word in the surface, but here it describes a flower in bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat a rival by going faster than them.

clue.text: Brought back from the French king shields

indicators.note: shields means protects by surrounding, so the king's word goes round the French one

parts.note: rex is Latin for king
du is French for 'from the' or 'of the'

explanation.surface: Shields carried home as spoils taken from the king of France.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin word placed after a name to mean restored or revived, as in a sequel's title.

clue.text: Eater of odd bits of guava orally infected

indicators.note: infected means corrupted or tainted, so the letters gathered before it are disturbed into a new order
odd bits of takes the first, third and fifth letters of guava

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who ate dodgy pieces of guava picked up an infection by mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits of' gives GAA, and 'infected' rearranges GAAORALLY. An eater is an apple for eating raw rather than cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: An eater is a dessert apple, and this is a popular sweet red variety from New Zealand.
